title: Some handfuls (Ruth 2)
hook: Boaz tells his workers to "let fall also some of the handfuls" for her

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ruth's vow, and the chesed she never named. Your line was thy people, my people. Today, the two women are home and need to eat.

The King James says it just happened: "her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz." Ruth goes out to glean, to pick up the stalks the reapers drop, which the Torah leaves for the poor and the stranger. She wanders into one field among many. The owner walks out from Bethlehem right then and greets his workers: "The LORD be with you." They call back: "The LORD bless thee." A boss and his reapers, blessing each other in the barley. Then he notices the stranger.
screen: `HER HAP WAS TO LIGHT ON THIS FIELD.` → `THE LORD BE WITH YOU.` → `HE NOTICES THE STRANGER.`

segments.voice: Boaz asks who she is, and hears: the Moabite girl who came back with Naomi. So he tells her: stay in my field, drink from the water my young men draw, I've told them not to touch you. Ruth falls on her face. "Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger?" His answer: I've heard everything you did for your mother-in-law, how you left your father and mother and the land you were born in. And he blesses her by the God "under whose wings thou art come to trust." At mealtime he hands her roasted grain; she eats her fill and has some left over, which she saves for Naomi. Then the line in today's title. When Ruth gets up to glean again, Boaz orders his reapers: "let fall also some of the handfuls of purpose for her, and leave them, that she may glean them, and rebuke her not." No sack handed over in front of everyone. He has the extra dropped on purpose where she'll find it, so it looks like ordinary gleaning, and she gathers it with her own hands. Rebuke her not: nobody stands over her. The gift is real, and her dignity stays whole. That evening she carries home so much barley that Naomi asks where she worked. Ruth says the name: Boaz. And the woman who came home empty says: "Blessed be he of the LORD, who hath not left off his kindness to the living and to the dead." Mara is blessing someone again.
screen: `WHY HAVE I FOUND GRACE, A STRANGER?` · `UNDER WHOSE WINGS THOU ART COME TO TRUST.` · then, large: `LET FALL SOME OF THE HANDFULS OF PURPOSE.` · then: `REBUKE HER NOT: DIGNITY KEPT.` · then: `THE EMPTY ONE BLESSES AGAIN.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who could use a little more but would hate to be handed charity, a neighbor living alone, a friend between jobs. Think like Boaz: how could a handful fall where they'll find it, food that happens to be left over, a ride offered as if it's on your way? If you pray, you can hold them under the wings Boaz spoke of.
Some handfuls. The grain Boaz has dropped on purpose for Ruth to glean, so the gift comes without shame. Today's word.
Your line: let fall some handfuls. A gift with nobody standing over it. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching on giving, rooted in the laws of leaving gleanings and the corners of the field, prizes gifts that protect the dignity of the one who receives, and the book of Ruth is read in synagogue on Shavuot.

chat.says: Why didn't Boaz just hand Ruth a sack of grain and be done with it?
options: He had extra dropped where she'd glean it, so the gift came without shame.
He worried his reapers would think he was wasting the harvest on her.
He didn't mean to help much; the extra grain just fell by accident.
chat.meaning: Boaz tells the reapers to let fall handfuls of purpose and rebuke her not, so Ruth gathers with her own hands and keeps her dignity.
